sanskrit: droṇa uvāca ity uktvā varadaḥ prādād varma tan mantram eva ca sa tena varmaṇā guptaḥ prāyād vṛtracamūṃ prati
english: Droṇa said: Having spoken thus, the boon-giver bestowed that armor together with its sacred spell; and guarded by that armor he went forth against the host of Vṛtra.

sanskrit: nānāvidhaiś ca śastraughaiḥ pātyamānair mahāraṇe na saṃdhiḥ śakyate bhettuṃ varmabandhasya tasya tu
english: Though floods of weapons of every kind were hurled down upon it in the great battle, the seam of that armor's binding could not be sundered.

sanskrit: tato jaghāna samare vṛtraṃ devapatiḥ svayam taṃ ca matramayaṃ bandhaṃ varma cāṅgirase dadau
english: Then the lord of the gods himself slew Vṛtra in battle, and that armor with its spell-wrought binding he gave to Aṅgiras.

sanskrit: aṅgirāḥ prāha putrasya mantrajñasya bṛhaspateḥ bṛhaspatir athovāca agniveśyāya dhīmate
english: Aṅgiras imparted it to his son Bṛhaspati, knower of the spell; and Bṛhaspati in turn declared it to the wise Agniveśya.

sanskrit: agniveśyo mama prādāt tena badhnāmi varma te tavādya deharakṣārthaṃ mantreṇa nṛpasattama
english: Agniveśya bestowed it upon me, and with it, O best of kings, I now bind on your armor with the spell, this day, for the guarding of your body.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evam uktvā tato droṇas tava putraṃ mahādyutiḥ punar eva vacaḥ prāha śanair ācāryapuṃgavaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Having spoken thus to your son, Droṇa of mighty splendor, that bull among teachers, softly addressed him with these further words.

sanskrit: brahmasūtreṇa badhnāmi kavacaṃ tava pārthiva hiraṇyagarbheṇa yathā baddhaṃ viṣṇoḥ purā raṇe
english: With the thread of Brahman I bind on your cuirass, O king, even as Hiraṇyagarbha bound it on Viṣṇu of old in battle.

sanskrit: yathā ca brahmaṇā baddhaṃ saṃgrāme tārakāmaye śakrasya kavacaṃ divyaṃ tathā badhnāmy ahaṃ tava
english: And as in the war over Tārakā the celestial cuirass of Śakra was bound on by Brahmā, so do I bind on yours.

sanskrit: baddhvā tu kavacaṃ tasya mantreṇa vidhipūrvakam preṣayām āsa rājānaṃ yuddhāya mahate dvijaḥ
english: Having bound on his cuirass with the spell according to rite, the brāhmaṇa sent forth the king to the great combat.

sanskrit: sa saṃnaddho mahābāhur ācāryeṇa mahātmanā rathānāṃ ca sahasreṇa trigartānāṃ prahāriṇām
english: Thus arrayed for war by the great-souled teacher, that mighty-armed one set out, attended by a thousand chariots of the smiting Trigartas,

sanskrit: tathā dantisahasreṇa mattānāṃ vīryaśālinām aśvānām ayutenaiva tathānyaiś ca mahārathaiḥ
english: and by a thousand rut-maddened, valor-flush elephants, by a myriad of horses, and by other great car-warriors as well.

sanskrit: vṛtaḥ prāyān mahābāhur arjunasya rathaṃ prati nānāvāditraghoṣeṇa yathā vairocanis tathā
english: Surrounded thus, the mighty-armed one advanced toward Arjuna's chariot amid the din of many instruments, even as the son of Virocana once marched forth.

sanskrit: tataḥ śabdo mahān āsīt sainyānāṃ tava bhārata agādhaṃ prasthitaṃ dṛṣṭvā samudram iva kauravam
english: Then arose a mighty clamor from your armies, O Bhārata, as they beheld the Kaurava host setting forth, fathomless as the ocean.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca praviṣṭayor mahārāja pārthavārṣṇeyayos tadā duryodhane prayāte ca pṛṣṭhataḥ puruṣarṣabhe
english: Saṃjaya said: When the Pārtha and the Vārṣṇeya had entered the field, O great king, and when Duryodhana, that bull among men, had set out behind them,

sanskrit: javenābhyadravan droṇaṃ mahatā nisvanena ca pāṇḍavāḥ somakaiḥ sārdhaṃ tato yuddham avartata
english: the Pāṇḍavas together with the Somakas rushed upon Droṇa with great speed and a mighty roar, and then the battle was joined.

sanskrit: tad yuddham abhavad ghoraṃ tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam pāñcālānāṃ kurūṇāṃ ca vyūhasya purato 'dbhutam
english: That battle between the Pāñcālas and the Kurus before the array grew terrible, tumultuous, hair-raising, and wondrous to behold.

sanskrit: rājan kadā cin nāsmābhir dṛṣṭaṃ tādṛṅ na ca śrutam yādṛṅ madhyagate sūrye yuddham āsīd viśāṃ pate
english: O king, never had we seen, nor ever heard of, such a battle as raged when the sun stood at midheaven, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnamukhāḥ pārthā vyūḍhānīkāḥ prahāriṇaḥ droṇasya sainyaṃ te sarve śaravarṣair avākiran
english: The Pārthas, led by Dhṛṣṭadyumna, their ranks marshaled and ready to strike, all together overwhelmed Droṇa's host with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: vayaṃ droṇaṃ puraskṛtya sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varam pārṣatapramukhān pārthān abhyavarṣāma sāyakaiḥ
english: We, placing Droṇa at our head, that best of all who bear arms, rained shafts upon the Pārthas led by the son of Pṛṣata.

sanskrit: mahāmeghāv ivodīrṇau miśravātau himātyaye senāgre viprakāśete rucire rathabhūṣite
english: Like two great clouds risen up with mingling winds at winter's end, the two hosts shone resplendent at the van, gleaming and adorned with chariots.

sanskrit: sametya tu mahāsene cakratur vegam uttamam jāhnavīyamune nadyau prāvṛṣīvolbaṇodake
english: Meeting, the two great armies wrought a surpassing onrush, like the rivers Gaṅgā and Yamunā in the rains, swollen with turbulent waters.

sanskrit: nānāśastrapurovāto dvipāśvarathasaṃvṛtaḥ gadāvidyun mahāraudraḥ saṃgrāmajalado mahān
english: With manifold weapons for its forward gale, thronged with elephants, horses, and chariots, its lightning the maces, terrible and vast, rose the great storm-cloud of battle.

sanskrit: bhāradvājāniloddhūtaḥ śaradhārāsahasravān abhyavarṣan mahāraudraḥ pāṇḍusenāgnim uddhatam
english: Driven up by the wind that was the son of Bharadvāja, bearing a thousand torrents of arrows, that most terrible cloud rained down upon the surging fire of the Pāṇḍava host.

sanskrit: samudram iva gharmānte vivān ghoro mahānilaḥ vyakṣobhayad anīkāni pāṇḍavānāṃ dvijottamaḥ
english: As a dread great wind blowing at the close of the hot season churns the sea, so did that best of brāhmaṇas throw the ranks of the Pāṇḍavas into turmoil.

sanskrit: te 'pi sarvaprayatnena droṇam eva samādravan bibhitsanto mahāsetuṃ vāryoghāḥ prabalā iva
english: They too, with every effort, charged straight at Droṇa, like mighty floods of water seeking to breach a great dam.

sanskrit: vārayām āsa tān droṇo jalaughān acalo yathā pāṇḍavān samare kruddhān pāñcālāṃś ca sakekayān
english: But Droṇa held them back, as a mountain holds back the floodwaters—the wrathful Pāṇḍavas in battle, and the Pāñcālas with the Kekayas.

sanskrit: athāpare 'pi rājānaḥ parāvṛtya samantataḥ mahābalā raṇe śūrāḥ pāñcālān anvavārayan
english: Then other kings as well, wheeling about on every side—mighty and heroic in battle—turned to check the Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: tato raṇe naravyāghraḥ pārṣataḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha saṃjaghānāsakṛd droṇaṃ bibhitsur arivāhinīm
english: Then in the battle that tiger among men, the son of Pṛṣata, together with the Pāṇḍavas, struck again and again at Droṇa, seeking to breach the enemy's host.

sanskrit: yathaiva śaravarṣāṇi droṇo varṣati pārṣate tathaiva śaravarṣāṇi dhṛṣṭadyumno 'bhyavarṣata
english: Even as Droṇa rained showers of arrows upon the son of Pṛṣata, so did Dhṛṣṭadyumna rain showers of arrows in return.

sanskrit: sanistriṃśapurovātaḥ śaktiprāsarṣṭisaṃvṛtaḥ jyāvidyuc cāpasaṃhrādo dhṛṣṭadyumnabalāhakaḥ
english: With swords for its forward gale, thronged with spears, darts, and lances, the bowstring its lightning and the twang of bows its thunder, rose the storm-cloud that was Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: śaradhārāśmavarṣāṇi vyasṛjat sarvatodiśam nighnan rathavarāśvaughāṃś chādayām āsa vāhinīm
english: He loosed torrents of arrows like a hail of stones in every direction, and striking down floods of chariots, horses, and the best of warriors, he covered the host.

sanskrit: yaṃ yam ārchac charair droṇaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ rathavrajam tatas tataḥ śarair droṇam apākarṣata pārṣataḥ
english: Whatever band of Pāṇḍava chariots Droṇa assailed with his shafts, from that very place the son of Pṛṣata drew Droṇa off with his arrows.

sanskrit: tathā tu yatamānasya droṇasya yudhi bhārata dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ samāsādya tridhā sainyam abhidyata
english: But while Droṇa strove thus in the fight, O Bhārata, his army, on encountering Dhṛṣṭadyumna, was split into three.

sanskrit: bhojam eke nyavartanta jalasaṃdham athāpare pāṇḍavair hanyamānāś ca droṇam evāpare 'vrajan
english: Some turned toward the Bhoja, others toward Jalasaṃdha, while still others, smitten by the Pāṇḍavas, fled straight to Droṇa.

sanskrit: sainyāny aghaṭayad yāni droṇas tu rathināṃ varaḥ vyadhamac cāpi tāny asya dhṛṣṭadyumno mahārathaḥ
english: And whatever ranks Droṇa, that best of car-warriors, mustered together, those Dhṛṣṭadyumna, the great car-warrior, scattered apart.

sanskrit: dhārtarāṣṭrās tridhābhūtā vadhyante pāṇḍusṛñjayaiḥ agopāḥ paśavo 'raṇye bahubhiḥ śvāpadair iva
english: The sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, broken into three, were slain by the Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas, like cattle without a herdsman in the forest set upon by many beasts of prey.

sanskrit: kālaḥ saṃgrasate yodhān dhṛṣṭadyumnena mohitān saṃgrāme tumule tasminn iti saṃmenire janāḥ
english: "Time itself is devouring the warriors, bewildered by Dhṛṣṭadyumna in that tumultuous battle"—so did men believe.

sanskrit: kunṛpasya yathā rāṣṭraṃ durbhikṣavyādhitaskaraiḥ drāvyate tadvad āpannā pāṇḍavais tava vāhinī
english: As the realm of a wicked king is harried by famine, sickness, and thieves, so was your host beset and driven into ruin by the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: arkaraśmiprabhinneṣu śastreṣu kavaceṣu ca cakṣūṃṣi pratihanyante sainyena rajasā tathā
english: As the sun's rays broke and flashed upon the weapons and the cuirasses, the eyes of the soldiers were dazzled and struck blind by that glare and by the dust.

sanskrit: tridhābhūteṣu sainyeṣu vadhyamāneṣu pāṇḍavaiḥ amarṣitas tato droṇaḥ pāñcālān vyadhamac charaiḥ
english: When his armies, split in three, were being slaughtered by the Pāṇḍavas, Droṇa, unable to bear it, then scattered the Pāñcālas with his shafts.

sanskrit: mṛdnatas tāny anīkāni nighnataś cāpi sāyakaiḥ babhūva rūpaṃ droṇasya kālāgner iva dīpyataḥ
english: As he crushed those ranks and struck them down with his arrows, the form of Droṇa became like the blazing fire of doomsday.

sanskrit: rathaṃ nāgaṃ hayaṃ cāpi pattinaś ca viśāṃ pate ekaikeneṣuṇā saṃkhye nirbibheda mahārathaḥ
english: Chariot and elephant and horse, and the foot-soldiers too, O lord of peoples—each one the great car-warrior pierced through with a single arrow in the fray.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavānāṃ tu sainyeṣu nāsti kaś cit sa bhārata dadhāra yo raṇe bāṇān droṇacāpacyutāñ śitān
english: Among the armies of the Pāṇḍavas there was not one, O Bhārata, who could withstand in battle the keen arrows loosed from Droṇa's bow.

sanskrit: tat pacyamānam arkeṇa droṇasāyakatāpitam babhrāma pārṣataṃ sainyaṃ tatra tatraiva bhārata
english: Scorched by the sun and seared by Droṇa's shafts, the host of the son of Pṛṣata reeled and wandered here and there, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tathaiva pārṣatenāpi kālyamānaṃ balaṃ tava abhavat sarvato dīptaṃ śuṣkaṃ vanam ivāgninā
english: And so too your force, harried by the son of Pṛṣata, blazed up on every side, like a dry forest set ablaze by fire.

sanskrit: vadhyamāneṣu sainyeṣu droṇapārṣatasāyakaiḥ tyaktvā prāṇān paraṃ śaktyā prāyudhyanta sma sainikāḥ
english: As the armies were cut down by the shafts of Droṇa and of the son of Pṛṣata, the soldiers, abandoning all thought of their lives, fought on with the utmost of their strength.

sanskrit: tāvakānāṃ pareṣāṃ ca yudhyatāṃ bharatarṣabha nāsīt kaś cin mahārāja yo 'tyākṣīt saṃyugaṃ bhayāt
english: Among your men and the foe alike as they fought, O bull of the Bhāratas, there was not one, great king, who forsook the battle out of fear.

sanskrit: bhīmasenaṃ tu kaunteyaṃ sodaryāḥ paryavārayan viviṃśatiś citraseno vikarṇaś ca mahārathaḥ
english: Bhīmasena, the son of Kuntī, his own brothers hemmed in—Viviṃśati, Citrasena, and Vikarṇa the great car-warrior,

sanskrit: vindānuvindāv āvantyau kṣemadhūrtiś ca vīryavān trayāṇāṃ tava putrāṇāṃ traya evānuyāyinaḥ
english: Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti, and the valiant Kṣemadhūrti—these three came as followers of those three sons of yours.

sanskrit: bāhlīkarājas tejasvī kulaputro mahārathaḥ sahasenaḥ sahāmātyo draupadeyān avārayat
english: The splendid king of the Bāhlīkas, nobly born and a great car-warrior, with his army and his counselors, held back the sons of Draupadī.

sanskrit: śaibyo govāsano rājā yodhair daśaśatāvaraiḥ kāśyasyābhibhuvaḥ putraṃ parākrāntam avārayat
english: Govāsana, the Śaibya king, with no fewer than a thousand warriors, held back the valiant son of Abhibhū, the king of Kāśi.

sanskrit: ajātaśatruṃ kaunteyaṃ jvalantam iva pāvakam madrāṇām īśvaraḥ śalyo rājā rājānam āvṛṇot
english: Ajātaśatru, the son of Kuntī, blazing like fire—him, the king, did Śalya, lord of the Madras, hold in check.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanas tv avasthāpya svam anīkam amarṣaṇaḥ sātyakiṃ prayayau kruddhaḥ śūro rathavaraṃ yudhi
english: But the unforbearing Duḥśāsana, having set his own division in array, advanced in wrath against Sātyaki, that hero and best of car-warriors, in the fight.

sanskrit: svakenāham anīkena saṃnaddhakavacāvṛtaḥ catuḥśatair maheṣvāsaiś cekitānam avārayam
english: I myself, with my own division, clad in fastened mail, with four hundred mighty archers, held Cekitāna in check.

sanskrit: śakunis tu sahānīko mādrīputram avārayat gāndhārakaiḥ saptaśataiś cāpaśaktiśarāsibhiḥ
english: And Śakuni with his division held back the son of Mādrī, with seven hundred Gāndhārakas armed with bows, darts, arrows, and swords.

sanskrit: vindānuvindāv āvantyau virāṭaṃ matsyam ārchatām prāṇāṃs tyaktvā maheṣvāsau mitrārthe 'bhyudyatau yudhi
english: Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti assailed Virāṭa of the Matsyas; those two great archers, ready to lay down their lives, rose up in battle for their friend's sake.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍinaṃ yājñaseniṃ rundhānam aparājitam bāhlikaḥ pratisaṃyattaḥ parākrāntam avārayat
english: Śikhaṇḍin, the son of Yajñasena, unconquered and pressing forward to bar the way—him the valiant did Bāhlika, fully arrayed, hold in check.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca pāñcālyaṃ krūraiḥ sārdhaṃ prabhadrakaiḥ āvantyaḥ saha sauvīraiḥ kruddharūpam avārayat
english: And Dhṛṣṭadyumna the Pāñcāla, together with the fierce Prabhadrakas—him, raging in form, the king of Avanti with the Sauvīras held back.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkacaṃ tathā śūraṃ rākṣasaṃ krūrayodhinam alāyudho 'dravat tūrṇaṃ kruddham āyāntam āhave
english: The heroic Ghaṭotkaca, that rākṣasa and cruel fighter, advancing in wrath upon the field—Alāyudha swiftly rushed against him.

sanskrit: alambusaṃ rākṣasendraṃ kuntibhojo mahārathaḥ sainyena mahatā yuktaḥ kruddharūpam avārayat
english: Alambusa, that lord of rākṣasas, raging in form—Kuntibhoja, the great car-warrior, joined by a mighty host, held in check.

sanskrit: saindhavaḥ pṛṣṭhatas tv āsīt sarvasainyasya bhārata rakṣitaḥ parameṣvāsaiḥ kṛpaprabhṛtibhī rathaiḥ
english: The lord of the Sindhus stood at the rear of the whole army, O Bhārata, guarded by supreme archers, by Kṛpa and the other car-warriors.

sanskrit: tasyāstāṃ cakrarakṣau dvau saindhavasya bṛhattamau drauṇir dakṣiṇato rājan sūtaputraś ca vāmataḥ
english: Two mightiest guardians of his wheels had the lord of the Sindhus: the son of Droṇa on his right, O king, and the son of the sūta on his left.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhagopās tu tasyāsan saumadattipurogamāḥ kṛpaś ca vṛṣasenaś ca śalaḥ śalyaś ca durjayaḥ
english: And as guardians of his rear there were, led by the son of Somadatta, Kṛpa and Vṛṣasena, Śala and the unconquerable Śalya.

sanskrit: nītimanto maheṣvāsāḥ sarve yuddhaviśāradāḥ saindhavasya vidhāyaivaṃ rakṣāṃ yuyudhire tadā
english: Wise in policy, mighty archers, all skilled in war—having thus arranged the protection of the lord of the Sindhus, they did battle then.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca rājan saṃgrāmam āścaryaṃ śṛṇu kīrtayato mama kurūṇāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca yathā yuddham avartata
english: Saṃjaya said: O king, hear of the wondrous battle as I recount it—how the combat of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas came to pass.

sanskrit: bhāradvājaṃ samāsādya vyūhasya pramukhe sthitam ayodhayan raṇe pārthā droṇānīkaṃ bibhitsavaḥ
english: Coming upon the son of Bharadvāja stationed at the front of the array, the Pārthas fought him in battle, seeking to breach Droṇa's division.

sanskrit: rakṣamāṇāḥ svakaṃ vyūhaṃ droṇasyāpi ca sainikāḥ ayodhayan raṇe pārthān prārthayanto mahad yaśaḥ
english: Guarding their own array, the soldiers of Droṇa likewise fought the Pārthas in battle, longing for great renown.

sanskrit: vindānuvindāv āvantyau virāṭaṃ daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ ājaghnatuḥ susaṃkruddhau tava putrahitaiṣiṇau
english: Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti struck Virāṭa with ten arrows, those two well-roused and seeking the welfare of your sons.

sanskrit: virāṭaś ca mahārāja tāv ubhau samare sthitau parākrāntau parākramya yodhayām āsa sānugau
english: And Virāṭa, O great king, sallying forth in valor, gave battle to those two valiant ones stationed in the fray, together with their followers.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ yuddhaṃ samabhavad dāruṇaṃ śoṇitodakam siṃhasya dvipamukhyābhyāṃ prabhinnābhyāṃ yathā vane
english: Their battle grew terrible, its waters running with blood, like the strife of a lion with two rut-streaming chief elephants in the forest.

sanskrit: bāhlīkaṃ rabhasaṃ yuddhe yājñasenir mahābalaḥ ājaghne viśikhais tīkṣṇair ghorair marmāsthibhedibhiḥ
english: Bāhlika, furious in the fight, the mighty son of Yajñasena struck with sharp, dreadful, barbless shafts that cleave the vitals and the bone.

sanskrit: bāhlīko yājñaseniṃ tu hemapuṅkhaiḥ śilāśitaiḥ ājaghāna bhṛśaṃ kruddho navabhir nataparvabhiḥ
english: And Bāhlika, sorely enraged, smote the son of Yajñasena hard with nine gold-shafted, stone-whetted arrows with bent knots.

sanskrit: tad yuddham abhavad ghoraṃ śaraśaktisamākulam bhīrūṇāṃ trāsajananaṃ śūrāṇāṃ harṣavardhanam
english: That battle grew terrible, thick with arrows and spears, breeding terror in the timid and swelling the joy of the brave.

sanskrit: tābhyāṃ tatra śarair muktair antarikṣaṃ diśas tathā abhavat saṃvṛtaṃ sarvaṃ na prājñāyata kiṃ cana
english: By the arrows loosed from those two, the sky and the quarters there were all so covered over that nothing whatever could be discerned.

sanskrit: śaibyo govāsano yuddhe kāśyaputraṃ mahāratham sasainyo yodhayām āsa gajaḥ pratigajaṃ yathā
english: Govāsana the Śaibya, with his host, gave battle to the great car-warrior, the son of Kāśi, as one elephant fights against another.

sanskrit: bāhlīkarājaḥ saṃrabdho draupadeyān mahārathān manaḥ pañcendriyāṇīva śuśubhe yodhayan raṇe
english: The king of the Bāhlīkas, enraged, fighting the great car-warriors who were the sons of Draupadī in the battle, shone like the mind contending with the five senses.

sanskrit: ayodhayaṃs te ca bhṛśaṃ taṃ śaraughaiḥ samantataḥ indriyārthā yathā dehaṃ śaśvad dehabhṛtāṃ vara
english: And they fought him fiercely with floods of arrows on every side, even as the objects of sense forever assail the body, O best of the embodied.

sanskrit: vārṣṇeyaṃ sātyakiṃ yuddhe putro duḥśāsanas tava ājaghne sāyakais tīkṣṇair navabhir nataparvabhiḥ
english: Sātyaki of the Vṛṣṇis your son Duḥśāsana struck in the fight with nine sharp arrows with bent knots.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho balavatā maheṣvāsena dhanvinā īṣan mūrchāṃ jagāmāśu sātyakiḥ satyavikramaḥ
english: Sorely pierced by that strong, mighty archer and bowman, Sātyaki of true valor swiftly sank into a faint for a while.

sanskrit: samāśvastas tu vārṣṇeyas tava putraṃ mahāratham vivyādha daśabhis tūrṇaṃ sāyakaiḥ kaṅkapatribhiḥ
english: But the Vārṣṇeya, recovering himself, swiftly pierced your son, that great car-warrior, with ten heron-feathered arrows.
